# pbs_prune_job (Resource)

Manages a PBS prune job.

Prune jobs automatically remove old backup snapshots based on retention policies. This helps 
maintain storage efficiency while ensuring important backups are retained according to your 
requirements. Configure retention using keep-last, keep-hourly, keep-daily, keep-weekly, 
keep-monthly, and keep-yearly parameters.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The unique identifier for the prune job.
- `schedule` (String) When to run the prune job. Uses systemd calendar event format (e.g., `daily`, `weekly`, `Mon..Fri *-*-* 02:00:00`).
- `store` (String) The datastore name where pruning will be performed.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) A comment describing this prune job.
- `disable` (Boolean) Disable this prune job without deleting it.
- `keep_daily` (Number) Keep daily backups for the last N days.
- `keep_hourly` (Number) Keep hourly backups for the last N hours.
- `keep_last` (Number) Keep the last N backup snapshots, regardless of time.
- `keep_monthly` (Number) Keep monthly backups for the last N months.
- `keep_weekly` (Number) Keep weekly backups for the last N weeks.
- `keep_yearly` (Number) Keep yearly backups for the last N years.
- `max_depth` (Number) Maximum depth for namespace traversal when pruning.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace filter as a regular expression. Only backups in matching namespaces will be pruned.

### Read-Only

- `digest` (String) SHA-256 digest of the PBS configuration file (prune.cfg) as of the last read. Informational only: it covers all objects in that file, changes on every write and is not used for locking.
